profile.headline: Software Engineer @ Cloudflare
profile.geoLocationName: New York, New York, United States
profile.summary: Hello! My name's Andy, and am a backend software engineer at Cloudflare in NYC! I previously worked at Lutron Electronics as a backend engineer for 3 years, specializing in our Go services. I graduated cum laude from Virginia Tech in 2022 with a major in Computer Engineering and a minor in Computer Science. When not pouring over Go change notes I like to whitewater kayak, bike around the city, play my drums, water my plants, fall off my mountain bike, fiddle with my servers, run marathons, and burn microcontrollers.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Working on Cloudflare Workers deployment (Go, Postgres, Kafka, S3, k8s, everything you can think of)
Somethings I've worked on so far: 
* Designed & rewrote the entire CI/CD, decreased pipeline times from 45 minutes to 10 minutes,
* Designed & implemented automated memory profiler for our Go services, used this resolve numerous runtime memory issues -- overloaded caches, overloaded S3 buffers, poorly behaving queries,
* Redesigned & rewrote massive volume distributed OLAP service for Durable Objects billing data. Increased throughput from 10 MB/s to >600 MB/s; designed & delegated implementation work for intern, 
* Serve on-call to handle team's inbounds and alerts -- had to deal with an internal team DDoSing us, amongst others.

positions.title: Sr. Software Engineer
positions.description:
Manage and maintain RESTful Golang server, gRPC database manager application, Python/Docker integration testing suite, and the accompanying CI/CD for consistent releases.

Oversee REST and gRPC API governance for business needs to maintain standards, best practices, documentation, and third party integration. Oversee and delegate merge authority for developers across all Go applications and integration testing suites.

Advise and enable business feature teams on technical design, documentation, and implementations.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Develop for and maintain RESTful Golang server for embedded Linux applications. 

Maintain Jenkins CI/CD for Go applications and Python/Docker integration test suite.

positions.title: Undergrad Research Assistant
positions.description: Implemented SPI & I2C IMU sensor array utilization for an STM32 in C for an animal husbandry data collection project.

positions.title: Firmware Engineering Intern
positions.description:
Researched, designed, and implemented a hard drive in situ log which described commands sent between the host computer and hard drives. 

Wrote driver code in C++ which enabled the hardware to begin logging commands (type, parameters, timestamp) and organize the data as it was dumped into memory.

Wrote TCL scripts to access the in-memory runtime data, and Python to process the data into a usable format for internal company tooling.


Resolved power and performance test issues by collecting and analyzing CI data and implementing fixes.

positions.title: Team member of SailBOT Design Team
positions.description: Lead a small team to implement motor controls for an autonomous sailboat. Designed and implemented an application specific servo wrapper and PID controlled rotary encoded DC motor. Oversaw implementation of RC controls and testing, and integrated subteam's work into design team's mainline.

positions.title: Software Engineering Intern
positions.description:
Designed and implemented a C++ to Python binding tool for use of legacy C++ in Python. Tool was used to streamline testing procedures to allow instantiation and utilization of C++ classes within Python. 
Communicated with client engineers to write and adhere to formal requirements, constraints and deadlines, as well as worked alongside co-intern to implement. 


Resolved UI bugs and designed interfaces using Qt in C++. Refactored displays for logical clarity and outlined aesthetics.

positions.title: Undergrad Research Assistant
positions.description:
Designed, built, tested and implemented a multiple channel temperature logging system using thermocouples and Arduinos for an experimental type of metal 3D printing.  

The collected data directly contributed to the published paper (with over 170 citations), which  can be found at https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2214860420307582
